speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are an infant experiencing recurrent stridor and wheezing; please know I will be gentle in my examination. To begin, can you tell me if these breathing difficulties happen specifically during feeding or when you cry?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: That combination of symptoms—specifically stridor and wheezing worsening with neck flexion, along with post-prandial vomiting—is highly suggestive of a vascular anomaly compressing the trachea. Can you tell me if you have ever noticed a visible lump or bulge on the side of his neck? REQUEST IMAGES: Neck_ultrasound.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. I also have Exacerbation during crying, Exacerbation during feeding, Exacerbation with neck flexion, Relief with neck extension, Occasional vomiting post-feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Laryngeal Web / Subglottic Stenosis
